guideTitle: Best Portable Jobsite Table Saws Under $400 (2026)
metaDescription: Five portable jobsite table saws under $400 compared on rip capacity, fence design, blade size, dado ability and the safety gaps budget saws leave.
expertTake: Under $400 a jobsite table saw is a 15-amp, 10-inch saw on a folding stand or an 8-1/4 inch compact, and the SKIL TS6307 is the best overall because it combines a 10-inch blade, a rack and pinion fence, a blade parallelism adjustment and a built-in folding stand. The DEWALT DWE7485 is the compact pick with 24.5 inches of rip and tool-free guarding, and the Evolution R10TS is the multi-material pick with a dado plate and sled. Skip this tier for cabinet-grade work, because budget fences and throat plates cannot hold a shop saw's tolerance.
introParagraphs: A table saw is the most useful and the most dangerous saw in a small shop, and the portable version trades the heavy cast iron table for lighter aluminum or plastic and a motor you can carry. That trade-off changes how it rips, how it stays square and how much of the safety work depends on you.

This guide explains what a low price buys in a jobsite table saw, how fence design, blade size and guarding change the daily experience, and where budget saws cut corners. The quick picks are above, and the reviews below show which saw fits which shop.

products.name: SKIL TS6307-00 10-Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Folding Stand, 15 Amp

specList.label: Alignment
specList.value: Micro-adjustment of blade to fence and miter slot

products.description:
The SKIL TS6307 is the best buy because it gets the three things that decide a table saw right: a 10-inch blade, a fence that stays parallel and a way to align the blade. A rack and pinion fence rides on rails and moves by a crank, so the fence stays parallel to the blade at every position. A fence that skews even a fraction of a degree pinches the board against the blade and invites kickback, which is why this feature matters more than motor size.

The parallel blade alignment micro-adjustment lets you square the blade to the miter slot and fence, and budget saws are often out of square from the factory. An integrated folding stand means legs fold in for storage and open in seconds, so the saw is ready to rip without a separate stand. Compared with the DEWALT DWE7485, the SKIL runs a larger blade and a bigger motor, while the DEWALT offers modular guarding.

A 10-inch blade cuts a full 2x4 on edge at 90 degrees in a single pass. Check the fence and blade alignment with a square and a test rip on arrival, and use the push stick for every narrow cut. The stock blade is a general-purpose blade, so swap in a combination or rip blade for better results.
products.bestFor: Homeowners and DIY builders who want a complete, stable 10-inch saw with a folding stand.
pros: Rack and pinion fence stays parallel to the blade
Blade micro-adjustment aligns to the miter slot
Integrated folding stand sets up quickly
10-inch blade cuts a full 2x4 on edge
cons: Budget aluminum table can flex on wide sheets
General-purpose blade leaves a rough edge

products.name: DEWALT DWE7485 8-1/4-Inch Compact Jobsite Table Saw, 15 Amp
products.description:
The DWE7485 is the compact saw with a name-brand guarding system. The Site-Pro modular guard comes off and goes back on without tools, which matters because a guard that is hard to remove is a guard that sits in the truck. It also offers 24.5 inches of rip capacity, enough to cut a 4x8 sheet of plywood down the middle with a little to spare.

It runs an 8-1/4 inch blade, smaller than the 10-inch saws, so its depth of cut is lower. That blade size is deliberate: a smaller blade makes the whole saw lighter and cheaper, and it is perfectly good for plywood, trim and shelving stock. A rack and pinion fence on telescoping rails keeps the fence parallel and extends for wide rips.

The trade is capacity: you will not rip a thick 4x4 in one pass. This is a saw for finish carpentry and cabinet panels, where its precise fence and guard are worth more than raw depth. Pair it with a stand, since the listing offers the saw alone, and keep the blade aligned.
products.bestFor: Finish carpenters and DIYers who want a light saw with a better guard and fence.
pros: Tool-free modular guard is easy to adjust and remove
Rack and pinion telescoping fence stays parallel
24.5 inches of rip handles plywood sheets
Light enough to carry with one hand
cons: 8-1/4 inch blade limits depth of cut
Sold without a stand on this listing
Cannot rip thick stock in one pass

products.name: Evolution R10TS 10-Inch Jobsite Table Saw, 15A, 26-Inch Rip, Dado Plate

specList.label: Included
specList.value: Zero-clearance throat plate, dado plate, cross-cut sled

products.description:
The Evolution R10TS is the table saw for people who cut more than wood. Its multi-material blade handles plastic, aluminum and mild steel, and the high-torque 15 amp motor includes a soft start that ramps the blade up gently instead of jerking the saw at power-on. A soft start is also kinder to a household circuit.

It includes a zero-clearance throat plate, a dado plate and a cross-cut sled, which is a surprisingly complete kit for the price. A zero-clearance plate has a narrow slot that supports the wood right at the blade, reducing tear-out on the bottom face. A dado plate allows a stacked dado set to cut grooves and rabbets, a capability many portable saws skip. Against the SKIL, the Evolution adds rip capacity of 26 inches and these accessories but lacks a stated folding stand.

Multi-material blades are a compromise. They cut metal, but they do not produce as smooth a finish in wood as a dedicated 40-tooth blade. Use the right blade for the job and keep a dust collection plan, since cutting metal throws chips.
products.bestFor: Makers who cut wood, plastic and light metal and want dado capability.
pros: 26 inch rip capacity
Soft start ramps up the blade smoothly
Includes dado plate and cross-cut sled
Multi-material blade cuts non-wood materials
cons: Multi-material blade is rougher in wood than a dedicated blade
Stand is not mentioned on this listing
Metal cutting needs extra safety care

products.name: WEN TT0811 8-1/4-Inch Compact Benchtop Table Saw, 11 Amp, 25-Inch Rip
products.description:
The WEN TT0811 is the budget compact. Its 11 amp motor spins an 8-1/4 inch 24-tooth blade up to 4,500 rpm, and a 25 inch rip capacity handles a 4x8 sheet down the middle. The depth of cut is 2.75 inches at 90 degrees and 2 inches at 45, enough for 2x lumber laid flat and most sheet goods.

A 24-tooth blade is a rip blade: it cuts fast and rough, and it needs replacement with a 40 or 60 tooth blade if you want a smooth edge on plywood. The motor, at 11 amps, is lighter than the 15 amp saws, so it will bog in thick hardwood. For softwood and plywood it is fine. Against the DEWALT, the WEN has a weaker motor but offers slightly more rip capacity.

Benchtop means it needs a table or a stand. Secure it to the bench with clamps, since a light saw can walk during a rip. Check the fence for parallelism with the miter slot on arrival, and keep your hands clear with a push stick.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a compact saw for plywood and softwood.
pros: 25 inch rip capacity for plywood sheets
Lightweight compact design
Depth of cut handles 2x lumber flat
Simple, low-cost entry saw
cons: 11 amp motor bogs in thick hardwood
24-tooth blade is rough without a swap

products.name: Prostormer 10-Inch Table Saw with Stand and Extendable Table, 15A
products.description:
The Prostormer is the all-in-one package: a 10-inch blade, a 15 amp motor, a stand and an extendable table. Its stated depth of cut, 3-1/2 inches at 90 degrees and 2-3/8 inches at 45, is the deepest in this guide, enough to cut through a 4x4 in one pass. The 5,000 rpm no-load speed is high, which gives clean cuts in thin stock.

The included stand makes it ready to use, and the extendable table supports longer boards. Compared with the SKIL, it offers a stand, a deeper stated cut and a faster blade, but it comes from a smaller brand with less support. The 24-tooth blade is a rip blade, so swap it for a finer one for plywood.

Because it is a no-name platform, check the guard, riving arrangement and fence alignment before first use, and do not run without the guard. Verify that the blade is parallel to the miter slot with a dial indicator or a careful measurement. For a first saw on a tight budget it is a good deal, as long as you treat setup as part of the purchase.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a stand, an extension and maximum depth in one purchase.
pros: Stated 3-1/2 inch depth cuts a 4x4 in one pass
Stand and extendable table included
15 amp motor with overload protection
Bevels 0 to 45 degrees
cons: 24-tooth rip blade is rough on plywood
Alignment and guard need careful setup

buyingCriteria.explanation: A rack and pinion fence moves on rails by a crank and stays parallel to the blade, as on the SKIL, DEWALT and Evolution. Cheap fences clamp at one end and can skew, which pinches the board and causes kickback. Test a fence by locking it and pushing the far end sideways; it should not move. A quick test is to set the fence at 10 inches, lock it, and measure from the blade to the fence at the front and back of the table, which should match within a hair.

A 10-inch blade, as on the SKIL, Evolution and Prostormer, cuts about 3-1/8 to 3-1/2 inches deep, enough for a 4x4. An 8-1/4 inch blade, as on the DEWALT and WEN, cuts about 2.75 inches. Choose 10-inch if you cut thick lumber and 8-1/4 inch for sheet goods. The DEWALT and WEN will ride on a table or bench, so plan for the bench height that gives you a comfortable stance.

Rip capacity is the distance from the blade to the fence's far end. The Evolution lists 26 inches, the WEN 25 and the DEWALT 24.5, all enough to split a 4x8 sheet into two halves. If you rip wide panels, check this figure carefully. Rip capacity matters most for wide panels, while narrow rips depend on the fence's accuracy.

The DEWALT's Site-Pro guard adjusts without tools, a real safety feature. No saw in this guide has flesh-sensing technology, so a push stick and a splitter or riving knife matter. Check each listing for a riving knife or splitter before you buy. Push sticks, featherboards and a splitter are the basic kit, and no saw replaces them.

A portable saw leaves the factory with some error, and the SKIL's blade micro-adjustment lets you correct it. Check the blade parallel to the miter slot with a square or dial indicator, and adjust. A misaligned blade burns wood and kicks back. Never skip the alignment check, especially on a new budget saw, because a blade off by even a small amount causes burning.

The SKIL's folding stand and the Prostormer's included stand make a saw ready to use, while the DEWALT and WEN need a stand. A stand adds cost and weight. If you use the saw in one place, a bench works, but a stand improves cutting height and stability. If you work outdoors, a stand with locking legs matters more than extra capacity.

specDecoder.meaning: Rip capacity is the widest cut to the right of the blade, set by the fence rails. A larger table means more support for the board but also more weight to carry.
specDecoder.watchFor: Some listings quote the total fence travel, not the usable distance. Compare 24 to 26 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: Depth of cut is the thickness of material the blade can cut at 90 and 45 degrees. Depth at 45 degrees matters when you cut bevels on thick stock.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 45 degree figure is smaller. The Prostormer lists 3-1/2 and 2-3/8 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: A geared fence that moves smoothly and stays parallel to the blade. A stand with wheels is nicer to move but adds cost.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check that the lock is solid, since a geared fence can still shift.

specDecoder.meaning: A circuit that ramps blade speed up gradually, reducing jerk and inrush current. Soft start also reduces the sudden torque jerk that can shift a light saw.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Evolution lists it here.

specDecoder.meaning: Amps measure motor current, a proxy for power. 15 amp is the household maximum on a 15 amp circuit. Household circuits are 15 amps, so a 15 amp saw leaves no room for other tools on the same circuit.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WEN's 11 amps is weaker than the 15 amp saws.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fence and alignment
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored rack and pinion fences and blade alignment features, since they decide accuracy. We read fence and alignment features closely because they predict accuracy better than motor size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade size, depth and rip capacity, giving the 10-inch saws credit for depth. We counted guard and safety features separately from convenience features.

howWeEvaluated.title: Guarding and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited tool-free guards and listed safety features, and noted the absence of flesh sensing. We compared depth of cut at both 90 and 45 degrees where listed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Kit contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted stands, dado plates, sleds and extensions that come in the box. We noted whether a stand is included, since it affects the true cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit across the lineup
howWeEvaluated.description: Each saw was placed by owner type, from plywood builders to metal and wood makers. We assumed a home builder who rips plywood and lumber.

howToChoose.intro: Match the saw to the work. Budget saws are best chosen by the work you do, since each trades something for its price.
howToChoose.note: A table saw is a rip saw first. Use a miter saw for crosscuts.

howToChoose.intro: Relative tiers in this group. Prices in this tier are close, so the features you get at each step matter more than the number.
howToChoose.note: The top tier adds guarding, not capacity.

howToChoose.intro: Blade size sets depth and weight. The biggest decision is blade size, since it sets depth, weight and cost.

howToChoose.intro: Budget saws have limits. A budget saw is for building, and a premium saw is for furniture.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a riving knife, a steady table and better dust control. A premium jobsite saw adds these.

cards.text: You cut a few sheets a year. The WEN or SKIL will do.

maintenance.why: Misalignment burns wood and causes kickback. Unplug before changing blades.
A smooth surface reduces friction and rust. A dirty fence rail causes drag.
A dull blade strains the motor. Wax prevents rust on the table.
A bent guard is unsafe. Replace a cracked throat plate.
Dust overheats the motor. Check the power cord for damage.

faq.q: Is a jobsite table saw safe?
faq.a: It can be, with a push stick, a guard and a splitter. No saw here has flesh sensing. Wear eye and ear protection and keep long sleeves and jewelry away from the blade.
A rip blade for lumber and a 40 to 60 tooth blade for plywood. Use a push stick for narrow rips, and never reach over the blade.
A 10-inch saw can in one pass. An 8-1/4 inch saw needs two passes. If a cut binds, shut the saw off and wait for the blade to stop before moving the board.
A stand improves stability and height. The SKIL and Prostormer include one.
Keep the fence parallel, use a splitter and never stand behind the blade.
The Evolution includes a dado plate. Others may not accept a dado set.
